title: Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading to amend the Singapore Sports Council Act, expanding SportSG's functions to include physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports, and updating its powers over standards, institutions and athlete support.
why_it_matters: The Bill expands what is legally recognised as sport to include mind sports and e-sports and physical fitness activities, and gives SportSG powers to set standards and establish athlete-training institutions. It also recognises the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner and increases the maximum SportSG Board size from 15 to 25. The Minister said the changes are to empower SportSG to more effectively administer its role in driving all Singaporeans to live better through sport.

key_points.point: The Acting Minister moved that the Bill be now read a Second time.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: That the Bill be now read a Second time

key_points.point: The Minister said the Singapore Sports Council Act has not been significantly updated since 1973 and needs updating to support SportSG's plans.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: To support these plans, we need to update the Singapore Sports Council Act, which has not been significantly updated since its enactment in 1973.

key_points.point: The Bill inserts new section 8(k) and (o) to give SportSG an enhanced mandate to establish institutions to develop and train national athletes, including consolidating the Singapore Sports School with the High Performance Sports Institute.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: new section 8(k) provides SportSG with the mandate to establish an institution formed that will be formed through consolidating the SSP with the High Performance Sports Institute.

key_points.point: The Bill inserts new section 8(m) and (n) to recognise SportSG's leadership role in raising capabilities and safety in the sports sector, including quality standards and codes of practice for coaching, equipment, facilities and accreditation.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: clause 6(h) of the Bill inserts a new section 8(m) and (n) to recognise the leadership role of SportSG in raising the capabilities and safety in the sports sector.

key_points.point: The Bill amends section 8(d) to recognise the Singapore National Paralympic Council as SportSG's key partner, as the Singapore National Olympic Council is recognised today.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: clause 6(b) of the Bill seeks to amend section 8(d) of the Act to recognise the Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) as SportSG's key partner, the same way Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) is recognised today.

key_points.point: The Bill amends section 2 to define "sports" to include mind sports and e-sports, and defines "mind sport" as a competitive game based on intellectual skill such as chess or bridge.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: clause 2 of the Bill seeks to amend section 2 of the Act to define "sports" to include mind sports and e-sports and to define "mind sport" as a competitive game based on intellectual skill such as chess or bridge.

key_points.point: The Bill amends section 8(a) to expand SportSG's functions to expressly include planning and promotion of physical fitness activities, in addition to sports, for competitive and recreational purposes.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Clause 6(a) of the Bill seeks to amend section 8(a) of the Act to expand the functions of SportSG to expressly include the planning and promotion of physical fitness activities, in addition to sports, for both competitive and recreational purposes.

key_points.point: The Bill increases the maximum size of SportSG's Board from 15 to 25 members.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 4 of the Act to increase the maximum size of SportSG's Board from 15 members to 25 members, so that more expertise could be brought onboard as needed.

key_points.point: The Bill updates SportSG's powers under section 9 to align them with its expanded functions under section 8.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Clause 7 of the Bill sets out a detailed list of updates to the powers of SportSG under section 9 of the Act, to align them with the expanded functions of SportSG in section 8 of the Act.

key_points.point: Mr Alex Yam said the Bill recognises that sport today is about inclusion, health, character, opportunity and lifelong participation, not just podiums and playing fields.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
key_points.quote: sport today is not just confine to podiums, pitches or to the playing fields.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked how a level playing field with the private sector would be ensured if SportSG both sets standards and manufactures equipment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: If SportSG is both the regulator in setting the standards and the supplier in manufacturing the equipment, how do we ensure a level playing field with the private sector?

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak sought assurance that new sports such as e-sports will complement rather than crowd out existing sporting pathways.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
key_points.quote: may I seek the assurance of the Minister that the Council will ensure that their development complements rather than crowds out existing sporting pathways

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik proposed that the maximum Council size remain at 15 members with expert sub-committees as needed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
key_points.quote: I therefore propose the following amendment that the maximum Council size remains unchanged at 15 members with provisions for establishing expert sub-committees as needed.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked whether the Government will extend retroactive support to past athletes who competed before current support programmes existed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
key_points.quote: Will the Government extend retroactive support to these past athletes who competed before such programme existed?

key_points.point: Ms Gho Sze Kee said the benchmark for supporting athletes should not be the number of medals won.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
key_points.quote: the benchmark of our support of our athletes should never be the number of medals they have won.

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San agreed with increasing the SportSG Board from 15 to 25 members.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
key_points.quote: I, therefore, agree with the amendment to increase the Board from 15 to 25 members.

key_points.point: Dr Charlene Chen asked how official recognition of e-sports will be implemented without normalising unhealthy screen habits, especially for vulnerable youths.
key_points.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
key_points.quote: how will official recognition of e-sports be implemented in a way that does not normalise unhealthy screen habits, especially for youths who are already vulnerable?

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked how SportSG will operationalise recognition of mind sports beyond the examples in the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
key_points.quote: how will SportSG operationalise recognition of mind sports beyond the examples in the Bill?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether accreditation powers could inadvertently create a pay-to-play system.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: Will these powers inadvertently create a "pay-to-play" system?

key_points.point: Ms Elysa Chen asked what governance structures will make new or consolidated institutions accountable to Parliament and the public.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: what governance structures will be put in place to ensure these new or consolidated institutions are accountable not just to SportSG, but to the Parliament and to the public?

key_points.point: Mr Lee Hong Chuang proposed a clear outcome-oriented resource framework that prioritises areas bringing the greatest social benefits.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
key_points.quote: establish a clear outcome-oriented resource framework, prioritising resources in areas that can bring the greatest social benefits.

key_points.point: Ms Joan Pereira said the amendments will help Singaporeans from all walks of life lead a more active lifestyle for better mental and physical health.
key_points.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
key_points.quote: The proposed amendments in this Bill will help Singaporeans from all walks of life lead a more active lifestyle for better mental and physical health.

key_points.point: The Minister said spexScholars' monthly stipends have recently been increased.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: We regularly review and have recently increased our spexScholars' monthly stipends.

key_points.point: The Minister assured that the consolidated entity will still be funded by the Government and accountable to MCCY and Parliament.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: the entity will still be funded by the Government and be accountable to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and Parliament.

key_points.point: The Minister said that for something to be considered a mind sport, it needs to be affiliated to an NSA, which is in turn affiliated to an International Federation.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: for something to be considered a mind sport, it needs to be affiliated to an NSA, who is in turn affiliated to an International Federation.

key_points.point: The Minister clarified that SportSG typically does not manufacture sports or physical fitness equipment for sale.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: SportSG typically does not manufacture sports or physical fitness equipment for sale.

key_points.point: The Minister said the target is to more than double registered coaches who can coach persons with disabilities, from 120 to 300 by 2030.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: We target to more than double the number of registered coaches under the National Registry of Coaches who can coach persons with disabilities, from 120 to 300 by 2030.

key_points.point: The Minister said the maximum of 25 Board members is a maximum, not a target.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: This is a maximum number, it is not a target, and we will continue to ensure that the Board runs effectively and efficiently.

key_points.point: The Minister said the Singapore Ice Skating Association has launched a request for proposal to develop and operate an ice rink and is reviewing proposals.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: The Singapore Ice Skating Association has since launched a request for a proposal to develop and operate an ice rink and is reviewing the proposals received.

key_points.point: The Minister said SportSG will work with industry, community partners and Government agencies like MOE and MOH on e-sports risks.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: We will work with industry and community partners such as the Singapore Cybersports and Online Gaming Association and the Singapore Esports Association, as well as Government agencies like MOE and MOH to do so.

key_points.point: The Minister said an expanded definition of sport does not mean all sports will be supported equally, given the need to use public funds wisely.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: an expanded definition of sport does not mean that we will support all sports equally given the need for us to use public funds wisely.

key_points.point: The Minister said support for sports is calibrated based on specific needs, governance standards and contribution to national sporting objectives.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: we calibrate the amount of support for sports based on their specific needs, governance standards and contribution to our national sporting objectives

what_happens_next: The Minister said, 'I seek to move.' The Chairman said the citation year '2025' will be changed to '2026', as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement. No further stage is stated.
not_said: Whether the Bill will be read a Second time or proceed to Committee stage is not stated.
How the expanded definition of mind sports will apply to specific games such as mahjong, poker or Pokemon cards is not resolved.
Whether funding for traditional sports will be diluted by support for e-sports and mind sports is not resolved.
Whether past athletes will receive retroactive support is not resolved.
Whether e-sports and mind sports athletes will have the same access to funding, facilities and national representation pathways as traditional sports athletes is not resolved.
Whether the maximum SportSG Board size will remain at 15 or be increased to 25 is not resolved.
Whether an ice rink will be built is not resolved.
Whether the Singapore National Olympic Council and the Singapore National Paralympic Council will merge is not resolved.
Whether accreditation will create a pay-to-play system is not resolved.
Whether new standards will impose burdens on small sports organisations and grassroots coaches is not resolved.
Whether the Bill will come into force and from what date is not stated.
